# Release Notes People Actually Read

**Logline:** A one-minute explainer for product managers on why release notes are ignored and how to fix them.

**STATUS: DRAFT v1. AWAITING EXPLICIT APPROVAL. No video, audio, asset or production work has started.**

**Runtime:** 1:00 (±10 s) | **Format:** 16:9, 1920x1080 | **Voice:** anonymous voice-over | **Spoken words:** about 100 | **Visuals:** rendered cards

**Legend (VISUAL column):** `SCENE` = what the viewer sees · `ON-SCREEN` = text, lower-thirds, captions · `DEMO` = the technical action being illustrated · `TRANSITION` = how we move on · `[BEAT]` = 0.5–1 s pause

**Source fidelity note:** All facts come from "Why Release Notes Get Ignored" (sample_source.txt). The survey figures (120 teams, one in five) are quoted as the source gives them; the authors say the sample was small and self-selected.

## Script

| TIMING | VISUAL | VO |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:15 | **SCENE:** A long list of release notes scrolls past, ordered by merge date.<br>**ON-SCREEN:** `1 in 5 customers opens them`.<br>**TRANSITION:** Hard cut. | Engineers write release notes. Almost nobody reads them. A survey of one hundred twenty teams found only one in five customers ever opens them. |
| 0:15–0:35 | **SCENE:** The same notes regroup into three headline cards.<br>**ON-SCREEN:** `SUMMARY · 3 HEADLINES · FULL LIST`.<br>**TRANSITION:** Cards slide left. | The fix is to group changes by user benefit. A short summary, three headline changes, and a link to the full list. [BEAT] Teams that did this doubled their open rate within two releases. |
| 0:35–0:50 | **SCENE:** A checklist builds line by line.<br>**ON-SCREEN:** `BENEFIT FIRST` · `ONE SENTENCE EACH` · `BREAKING CHANGES FIRST`.<br>**TRANSITION:** Checklist fades. | Start with the benefit, not the ticket number. One sentence per entry. Put breaking changes first, and have someone who did not write the code review the notes. |
| 0:50–1:00 | **SCENE:** End card on a plain background.<br>**ON-SCREEN:** `Try it on your next release`.<br>**TRANSITION:** Fade to black. | Try it on your next release, and tell us what changes in your support queue. |
